q: The first three terms of a geometric sequence are $3k+4,\ \ 12-3k,\ \ k+16$. The sequence converges. Find $k$, and the sum to infinity.

lines.say: Three terms of a geometric sequence, all in terms of k. {cv}The sequence converges. Find k, and the sum to infinity.
This is a real Edexcel A-level question. Pause and have a go!
Okay! In a geometric sequence, you multiply by the same ratio each time, {r}so the middle term squared equals the other two multiplied.
Expand and tidy up, {quad}and you get three k squared, minus sixty-two k, plus forty, equals zero.
That factorises, {roots}so k is twenty, or two thirds.
Which one? {k23}With two thirds, the terms are six, ten, sixteen and two thirds. {r23}The ratio is five thirds, so it blows up.
{k20}With twenty, it's sixty-four, minus forty-eight, thirty-six. {r20}The ratio is minus three quarters, so it converges. {k}So k is twenty.
Sum to infinity is a over one minus r. {s}Sixty-four over seven quarters, {ans}which is two hundred and fifty-six sevenths.
And keep it as a fraction! {trap}The mark scheme doesn't accept thirty-six point six.
